attempts.summary:
I fixed the test setup in all 13 disputed tests, changing only test_chongdae.py and test_concurrency.py. No hook, engine or normalizer code changed, and no hook assertion was weakened.

F1 (the 7 hook tests): the shared `hook()` helper now builds its env with a new `session_env(**env)`. That function copies os.environ, applies the given keys and removes any key passed as None. Each hook call in the seven tests now passes `**NORMAL_SESSION` (`{"AGENT_WORKER": None}`). The direct session_start subprocess in test_performed_by_is_recorded_like_an_author_line gets `env=session_env(**NORMAL_SESSION)`. The worker-suppression asserts still set `AGENT_WORKER="1"` themselves, and os.environ is never cleared. Other tests call `hook()` exactly as before, so they behave the same.

F2 (the 6 command expectations): each expectation now builds the form the engine actually records instead of the raw sys.executable:
- writer, quibble and verifier requests and records: `chongdae.portable_argv(...)`, or `shlex.join(portable_argv(...))` where the record holds a joined string.
- `did` records: a new `did_command(argv, target)`. It joins `neutral_path` of each argument and runs `public_projection` over the result. That is how `cmd_did` writes them: `outside_argv` uses `neutral_path`, so a `/tmp` interpreter becomes `'<tmp>'`, not just a `~` path.
- the concurrency public task file: `public_projection(portable_argv(...), project)`. test_concurrency.py now imports chongdae from beside the engine to do this.

Verified with `<tmp>`: all 13 pass in all four combinations — with ~/.local/bin/python3.11 (under HOME) and with <tmp> (outside HOME), each with AGENT_WORKER=1 and without it.

The request's checks pass: test_public_projection.py, test_record_transactions.py and test_state_recovery.py exit 0, and the prior-work hash check lists no changed files. The full test_concurrency.py passes.

The full test_chongdae.py has 1 failure, which was already there: test_a_landed_worktree_run_records_the_merge_commit fails with `FileNotFoundError: '<tmp>'`. It fails the same way with the unamended HEAD test file, run from a copy outside the tree. It is the projected worktree-main close lock that this goal's projection contract is meant to fix, so I left it alone.
non-claims: As the amendment expects, the corrected tests pass now; none of them is red before a build.

These test names do not contain the section id (F1/F2): the amendment names existing tests, and renaming them would change other tests' identity. So a check cannot select them by section id, only by name.

The F2 expectations are built with the engine's own helpers (portable_argv, neutral_path, public_projection), as the brief allows. So they check that the recorded command matches that projection of the given argv. They cannot catch a bug inside those helpers; test_public_projection.py covers that.

test_chongdae.py::test_a_landed_worktree_run_records_the_merge_commit fails (FileNotFoundError '<tmp>') both with and without this amendment, outside HOME with AGENT_WORKER=1. It is not one of the 13 and was not changed.
Checked only on macOS with Python 3.11 (~/.local/bin/python3.11 and the <tmp> link); not on Windows or another Python version.

disputed-tests.why: Contract R6 (added after this amendment): a task's checks (def.checks, checks) are executable argv and keep the portable form portable_argv gives them at add; the narrow projection does not apply to them. test_concurrency.ConcurrentCommands.test_check_attachment_is_not_lost_during_another_run now expects def.checks == [public_projection(portable_argv([sys.executable, '-c', 'pass']), project)[0]]; under R6 the expected public form is [portable_argv([sys.executable, '-c', 'pass'])]. The two differ when the interpreter's path is under a temporary directory (<tmp> gives '<tmp>' today but must stay the path). Change only that expectation; the F1/F2 amendment otherwise stands. It may fail before privacy-build-2 is built (today's engine still projects checks).

attempts.summary:
I changed the one disputed expectation and left the rest of the earlier F1/F2 amendment as it was. The fix is correct by R6, but the test still fails on today's engine when the interpreter is under /tmp, which is what the dispute predicted.

The disputed check is test_concurrency.ConcurrentCommands.test_check_attachment_is_not_lost_during_another_run. It used to expect `def.checks == [public_projection(portable_argv([sys.executable, '-c', 'pass']), project)[0]]`. It now expects `def.checks == [portable_argv([sys.executable, '-c', 'pass'])]`. The test was wrong and the builder read the contract correctly. R6 says a task's checks "are not narrowed by the projection: they keep the portable form portable_argv gives them when the task is added". Nothing else in either file changed; the diff is two lines in test_concurrency.py.

I ran it with <tmp> with <tmp> on PATH, with AGENT_WORKER=1 and without it:
- **~/.local/bin/python3.11 (under HOME):** passes.
- **<tmp> (outside HOME):** fails. It expects `[['<tmp>', '-c', 'pass']]`, but today's engine still applies the narrow projection to checks. It should pass once privacy-build-2 is built.
non-claims: The builder's dispute is correct and the test was wrong. R6 says: "A task's checks ... are not narrowed by the projection: they keep the portable form portable_argv gives them when the task is added". The expectation now follows that sentence.

The corrected test fails on today's engine when the interpreter is outside HOME (<tmp>), because the engine still narrows checks. It passes under ~/.local/bin/python3.11, where there is no temp prefix to tell the two forms apart.
The test name does not contain the section id (R6/F). It is an existing test, so a check selects it by name.
The expectation is built with the engine's own portable_argv, so it cannot catch a bug inside portable_argv itself.
I did not re-run the other 12 tests from the earlier amendment; they were not changed in this pass.
